newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian copper extends losses, other metals steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian copper extends losses, other metals steady.

text.p: Indian copper prices extended losses on Tuesday but zinc staged a recovery, traders said.
They said other base metals were steady in light trade.
Copper prices fell further by 100 rupees to 12,900 rupees per quintal on selling by stockists following reports of a reduction in prices by state-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd.
Copper was down 100 rupees on Saturday and 150 rupees last week.
Sluggish industrial demand also subdued market sentiment, traders said.
Hindustan Copper Ltd. has reduced selling prices by 2,000 rupees per tonne for the second half of August, they said.
Zinc prices rose 150 rupees to 8,550 rupees per quintal on speculative buying on expectations state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd. may announce a hike in prices, traders said.
"The market is agog with rumours that Hindustan Zinc Ltd. may hike selling prices by 1,500/2,000 rupees per tonne," said Sharad Parikh, a leading dealer.
"We are awaiting an official announcement from the company," he said.
Tin and nickel were unchanged at lower levels on stray industrial support and steady supplies, traders said.
Tin ended at 28,500 rupees per quintal after losing 500 rupees last week while nickel was steady at 32,800 rupees per quintal after losing 1,000 rupees last week.
Other metals which were steady were lead and aluminium at 4,200 and 7,800 rupees per quintal respectively, traders said.
